questions.solution: The erroneous part is 'on.' In the erroneous part, the use of the preposition 'on' is wrong as the verb 'wait' is in the base form. We need to use 'to' before the base form of the verb. Correct sentence: I told Rahu to wait for two hours at the bus stop.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. They was / celebrating their / Silver wedding anniversary / next month in Dubai.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

They was / celebrating their / Silver wedding anniversary / next month in Dubai.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. They was .

Key Points

  • The given sentence contains a grammatical error in the first segment, "They was".
  • The subject "They" is plural, and therefore, the correct verb form is "were", not "was".
  • Correct grammar usage would be: "They were".
  • The other segments of the sentence are grammatically correct.

Correct sentence: They were celebrating their Silver wedding anniversary next month in Dubai.

Additional Information

  • The use of "next month" indicates a future event, but in this case, the verb tense remains in the past progressive (were celebrating) to describe an intention or plan in informal usage.
  • Subject-verb agreement: Always match the verb form to the subject in terms of number (singular or plural).

questions.question: The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. If I was a king, I would have tried my best to remove poverty from my country.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

If I was a king, I would have tried my best to remove poverty from my country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence contains a grammatical error in the conditional clause "If I was a king."
  • When expressing hypothetical or unreal situations, the verb "was" should be replaced with "were" in the clause following "if."
  • The correct phrasing is "If I were a king," which aligns with the subjunctive mood used for hypothetical conditions.
  • This correction ensures the sentence is grammatically accurate and conveys the intended meaning properly.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "If I were a king, I would have tried my best to remove poverty from my country."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "on my country" – This is incorrect as the correct preposition to use is "from" in this context.
  • Option 2: "my best by remove poverty" – This is grammatically incorrect as "by remove" should be replaced with "by removing."
  • Option 4: "I would has tried" – This is grammatically incorrect as "has" should be replaced with "have" in this context.

questions.question: Select the option that corrects the error in the given sentence. She sings good.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that corrects the error in the given sentence.
She sings good.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. well.

Key Points

  • The word "good" means having the required qualities, or of a high standard. (अच्छा)
    • Example: She is a good person who always helps others.
  • "Well" refers to performing an action in a good or satisfactory way. It is the adverb form used to describe how an action is performed. (अच्छी तरह)
    • Example: She sings well in the choir.
  • Hence, we can infer that the correct word to use in the sentence is 'well' instead of 'good'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. well.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Better (बेहतर): Comparative form of good, meaning of a higher standard or quality.
    • Example: Her singing has improved and is much better now.
  • Best (सर्वोत्तम): Superlative form of good, meaning of the highest quality.
    • Example: She is the best singer in the competition.
  • Goodly (विशाल): An archaic or literary term meaning large in size or quantity.
    • Example: He donated a goodly sum to charity.

questions.question: Direction: The given sentence is divided into four parts. Select the option that contains an error. The Dutta company/ has not being making/ new school bags/ since the lockdown commenced.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: The given sentence is divided into four parts. Select the option that contains an error.

The Dutta company/ has not being making/ new school bags/ since the lockdown commenced.
questions.solution: The correct form of the verb in this sentence should be "been" instead of "being." "Being" is a present participle form of the verb which is not appropriate in this context. The verb "been" is the past participle form of the verb "be" and is used to indicate a state or condition that started in the past and continues up to the present. Example: Bucky has been out for a long time.

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. He was surprised at me refusing his offer.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

He was surprised at me refusing his offer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is at me refusing

Key Points

  • 'at my refusing' should be there in place of 'at me refusing'
  • Possessive case of pronoun comes before gerund for the following reason:
    • The failure to use the possessive case with the gerund can create an illogical statement
    • Consider the following sentence:
      • I appreciate you taking time to talk with me about the project.
        ​The possessive case of you is not used with the gerund taking, so the writer ends up making the illogical statement (at least in this context) “I appreciate you.” The point is not that the writer of the sentence appreciates you, per se; instead, the writer appreciates the fact that you took time to discuss the project: ​​
      • I appreciate your taking time to talk with me about the project.​​​​​​

Thus, the correct sentence is: He was surprised at my refusing his offer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. What are the options available of me for a change of career?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

What are the options available of me for a change of career?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'options available to me'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'options available to me' should be used instead of 'options available of me'.
  • The adjective 'available' should be followed by 'to' in the given context.
  • It means '(used about things) that you can get, buy, use, etc. उपलब्‍ध, (वस्‍तुएँ)'.
    • Example: This information is easily available to everyone at the local library.
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 1.
     

Correct Sentence: What are the options available to me fir a change of career?

Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
  • यहाँ, 'options available of me'. के स्थान पर 'options available to me' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
  • दिए गए संदर्भ में adjective 'available' के बाद 'to' होना चाहिए।
  • इसका अर्थ है '(चीजों के बारे में प्रयुक्त) जो आप प्राप्त कर सकते हैं, खरीद सकते हैं, उपयोग कर सकते हैं, आदि'।
    • Example: This information is easily available to everyone at the local library.
  • इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर विकल्प 1 है।

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. Mr. Rao asked the newcomer / to his office / if he will minded / working late that day.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

Mr. Rao asked the newcomer / to his office / if he will minded / working late that day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2) i.e., 'if he will minded'.

Key Points

  •  From the given sentence it is evident that Mr. Rao is enquiring about the future work conditions.
  • "if he will minded" is an incorrect phrase as minded is in the past tense form. 
  • We need to use the base form of "mind" for the sentence because we know that whenever we use the modal verb we always use the base form of the verb with it.
  • To change the 'if clause' into the past tense, 'will' has to be changed into 'would' followed by the first form of verb 'mind'
  • So, the error lies in segment 3 of the sentence, making option 2 the correct answer. 

Correct sentence - Mr. Rao asked the newcomer / to his office / if he would mind working late that day.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The supervisor / wanted to known / the pros and cons / of the issue.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The supervisor / wanted to known / the pros and cons / of the issue.
questions.solution:
The error is in "wanted to known".

Key Points

  • 'Wanted to known' is grammatically incorrect.
  • The correct usage is 'know' instead of 'known'.
  • To know = the infinitive form
  • known = the past participle form
  • Examples-
    • I know her name.
    • I have known her for a long time.
  • The correct sentence: The supervisor wanted to know the pros and cons of the issue.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. The director wanted Aziz to play the role of the doctor as well also that of the apprentice.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

The director wanted Aziz to play the role of the doctor as well also that of the apprentice.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- as well as​.

Key Points

  • An adverb is a word or phrase that modifies or qualifies an adjective, verb, or other adverb or a word group, expressing a relation of place, time, circumstance, manner, etc.
  • As well is an adverb which means ‘also’, ‘too’ or ‘in addition’. We usually use 'as well' at the end of a clause.
  • As well as is a multi-word preposition which means ‘in addition to’.
  • Example:
    • We look forward very much to seeing you again and to meeting your wife as well.
    • When they go to Austria, they like walking as well as skiing.
  • As per the structures given above, the adverb 'as' will replace 'also' in the 1st option.
     

Correct Sentence: The director wanted Aziz to play the role of the doctor as well as that of the apprentice.

 ​​​​Additional Information  

  • The adverb 'there' is used to begin some stories written in a traditional style.
  • Example:
    • There once lived a poor widow who had a beautiful daughter.

questions.question: Directions: Identify the segment in the sentence given below which contains a grammatical error. The old woman in our locality is knowing for her hot temper.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Identify the segment in the sentence given below which contains a grammatical error.

The old woman in our locality is knowing for her hot temper.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'is knowing for'.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the use of the gerund form of the verb 'knowing' is incorrect.
  • The given sentence is in the present simple tense of the passive voice.
  • The present simple passive format is "is + V3 (known)".
  • Therefore, the past participle form of the verb 'known' should be used in place of 'knowing'.


Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct Sentence: The old woman in our locality is known for her hot temper.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error. Ms. Malathi is old much to join a college now.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.

Ms. Malathi is old much to join a college now.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. old much .

Key Points

  • The phrase 'old much' in the sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • In English, adjectives of age, like "old," are modified by the adverb 'too' (e.g., "too old").
  • The correct phrase should be 'too old' instead of 'old much'.
  • The corrected sentence would read: "Ms. Malathi is too old to join a college now."

Correct sentence: Ms. Malathi is too old to join a college now.

Additional Information

  • Common Errors in Adjective Usage:
    • Using adverbs like 'much' or 'very' incorrectly with adjectives.
    • For example, we say "too old," "very old," or "extremely old," but not "old much."
  • When to Use 'Too':
    • 'Too' is used to indicate excessiveness and is followed by an adjective or adverb.
    • Example: "The bag is too heavy to carry."

questions.question: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. He went to work but returned back immediately.
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

He went to work but returned back immediately.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.

The error is in the part 'but returned back'.

It is redundant to use 'back' after 'returned'. The word 'back' is implied by the word 'returned'.

Thus the correct sentence will be: He went to work but returned immediately.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’. This film is a non-stop riot that many cite as one of the funny films of all time.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’.

This film is a non-stop riot that many cite as one of the funny films of all time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2)

Key Points

  • The sentence is trying to convey that the film is renowned for being one of the most humorous films ever made.
  • The correct comparative form to use in this context should be the superlative form "funniest" instead of the positive form "funny".
  • ​When comparing three or more items, we use the superlative form.
  • For adjectives with one or two syllables, we typically add '-est' to the adjective (e.g., funny → funniest).
  • Examples:
    • This is the most beautiful garden I have ever seen.
    • She is the smartest student in the class.

Therefore, the correct statement is "This film is a non-stop riot that many cite as one of the funniest films of all time."

Additional Information

  • Other options are incorrect:
    • "No rectification needed" is incorrect because the sentence needs a superlative form.
    • "More funny" is incorrect because it is not the correct form of comparison.
    • "Funnier" is incorrect because it is the comparative form and not the superlative.

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error. He is the same man which I saw yesterday at the gate.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error.

He is the same man which I saw yesterday at the gate.
questions.solution:
One should have a basic knowledge of pronouns to understand this question.

Remember,

We use which to refer to a thing or an idea, and to ask about choices.

For eg:

           My car, which is 20 years old, isn't worth much.

When who is the object of a verb, whom can be used instead,

For eg:

           The person to whom you are referring no longer works here.

In the given sentence, he is the object of the verb saw, so whom will be used.

Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. I am sure / that he will praying / for a good crop / this year.
questions.questionHtml:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error.

I am sure / that he will praying / for a good crop / this year.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: that he will praying. The phrase "that he will praying" is incorrect. It should be "that he will be praying" to correctly use the future continuous tense.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. We must prayed at the Almighty for the well-being of all family members.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

We must prayed at the Almighty for the well-being of all family members.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'pray to'.Key Points  
 

  • The error lies incorrect usage of the second form of the verb after the modal verb must.
  • The modal verb must is used to express obligation and necessity and it is usually followed by an infinitive without ‘to’.
  • Example:
    •   I must stop smoking. It’s really bad for my health.
  • Thus, 'pray to' will be used in place of 'prayed'.

Correct sentence: We must pray to the Almighty for the well-being of all family members.

Additional Information 
  

  • Modal verb: an auxiliary verb that expresses necessity or possibility.

 

Hinglish Answer:

सही उत्तर 'pray to' है।
 
Key Points
  • Modal verb must के बाद त्रुटि 2nd form of verb का गलत उपयोग है।
  • Modal verb must का उपयोग अनिवार्यता (obligation) और आवश्यकता (necessity) को व्यक्त करने के लिए किया जाता है और इसके बाद आमतौर पर infinitive बिना ‘to’ आता है।
    • उदाहरण: I must stop smoking. It’s really bad for my health.
    • इस प्रकार, 'prayed' की जगह 'pray to' का उपयोग किया जाएगा।
सही वाक्य: We must pray to the Almighty for the well-being of all family members.
 
Additional Information
  • Modal verb: एक auxiliary verb जो अनिवार्यता या संभाव्यता को व्यक्त करता है।

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No improvement'. One evening, when father was coming home from work, I played in the front garden.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No improvement'.

One evening, when father was coming home from work, I played in the front garden.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. was playing.

  • The speaker is talking about something that occurred in the past while another action was happening. The other action was 'father was coming home' and at the same time the speaker was playing.
  • Here we need to use the past continuous tense for something that was happening in the past.
  • 'Played' is used in the simple past tense.
  • Eg- I played football yesterday.

We will use 'was playing' instead of 'played' to make the sentence correct.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into three segments. One of them may contain an error. Select the option that has the segment with the error. If you don’t find any error, select ‘No error’ as your answer. Mr. Ali’s shop / is further to / the hospital.
questions.questionHtml: The following sentence has been divided into three segments. One of them may contain an error. Select the option that has the segment with the error. If you don’t find any error, select ‘No error’ as your answer. Mr. Ali’s shop / is further to / the hospital.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The error lies in the phrase "is further to".
  • The correct word should be 'Farther' instead of 'Further' as the sentence is talking about the distance.
  • The word "farther" is not used with the preposition "to" when indicating distance.
  • The correct preposition in this context is "from" to indicate comparative distance.
  • Hence, the correct expression should be "Mr. Ali’s shop is farther from the hospital."
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "Mr. Ali’s shop is farther from the hospital."

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The manager / did not / gone to / Bombay yesterday.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The manager / did not / gone to / Bombay yesterday.
questions.solution: Replace "gone" with "go" to correct the sentence. Gone is the third form of the verb "Go". The structure should be: Subject + didnot+ v1+ object. Corrected sentence: The manager did not go to Bombay yesterday.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer. The project was completed / more quicker / than expected.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

The project was completed / more quicker / than expected.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: more quicker.

The phrase "more quicker" is incorrect because "quicker" is already the comparative form of "quick." The correct phrase should be "more quickly."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Her paintings are way better then her sketches.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

Her paintings are way better then her sketches.
questions.solution: The correct substitution for the underlined segment "then" in the given sentence is "than" because we are comparing her paintings with her sketches. "Then" is used to indicate time, while "than" is used for comparisons. Therefore, option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My elder brother,/ which you’ll / meet later,/ is a dentist.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My elder brother,/ which you’ll / meet later,/ is a dentist.
questions.solution: Here, 'whom you'll' should be used instead of 'which you'll'. 'Whom' is 'used instead of ‘who’ as the object of a verb or preposition'. Example: Whom did you meet there?

questions.question: Direction: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. My younger brother were attending a short-term computer course these days.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

My younger brother were attending a short-term computer course these days.
questions.solution: The error in the original sentence is the use of "were attending." The context indicates a current activity, we should use the present tense. Since the sentence is referring to a present action, it should use the singular form "is attending" instead of the plural "were attending." Correct sentence: My younger brother is attending a short-term computer course these days.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Huda lived in / the southern part / off Germany.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Huda lived in / the southern part / off Germany.
questions.solution: The error lies in the part 'off Germany.' In the given sentence, the correct preposition to use is "of" instead of "off." "Of" is a preposition that indicates the relationship between two things, such as possession, origin, or cause.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The new / secretary / does not likes / me.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The new / secretary / does not likes / me.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: 3) does not likes. The phrase "does not likes" is grammatically incorrect. The correct form is "does not like" because 'does' is already a helping verb and the main verb should be in its base form.

questions.question: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. No sooner did we receive your message when we heaved a sigh of relief.
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

No sooner did we receive your message when we heaved a sigh of relief.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.

The error is in the phrase 'when we heaved'.

The given sentence is a conditional sentence. 'No sooner' is always followed by 'than'.

'When' must be replaced with 'than'.

The correct sentence will be: No sooner did we receive your message than we heaved a sigh of relief.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The new/ smartphone is/absolutely best than/ the latest model.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The new/ smartphone is/absolutely best than/ the latest model.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the adjective "best" instead of the comparative form "better."
  • Comparative adjectives are used to compare differences between the two objects they modify (larger, smaller, faster, higher).
  • The correct phrase should be "absolutely better than," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
  • Thus, the error is located in part 3 of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "The new smartphone is absolutely better than the latest model."
 
Additional Information
  • 1: "The new" – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • 2: "smartphone is" – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • 4: "the latest model." – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • No error – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 3.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Ishita will playing Tennis for her favourite team.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Ishita will playing Tennis for her favourite team.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: will playing.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the phrase 'will playing' is incorrect.
  • The phrase "will playing" is incorrect because "will" should be followed by the base form of the verb, which is "play."
  • The correct phrase is "will play," indicating future tense.
  • Hence, 'will play' must replace 'will playing' to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: Ishita will play Tennis for her favourite team.

questions.question: The given sentence contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment that contains the error. I will join you tomorrow if I will have time.
questions.questionHtml:
The given sentence contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment that contains the error.

I will join you tomorrow if I will have time.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is 'will have time'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • The given sentence is an example of the first conditional.
  • In type 1 conditional sentences, the tense in the "if" clause is the simple present tense, and the tense in the main clause is the simple future or the simple future.
  • If clause(condition) Main clause(result)
    If + simple present simple future
    If my father doesn't pick me up I'll take the bus home.
  • Example: 
    • If he works hard, he will surely get the job. 
    • If he works hard, he would surely get the job.
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 2. 
     

Correct Sentence: I will join you tomorrow if I have time.

questions.question: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. People has been warning in advance about the coming economic crisis.
questions.questionHtml:
In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.

People has been warning in advance about the coming economic crisis.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'has been warning'.

Key Points

  • According to the subject-verb agreement rule, if the subject is singular, the verb must be singular and if the subject is plural, the verb must also be plural. 
  • Examples, 
    • These clothes are too small for me.
    • People travel overseas these days.
    • Some people were hurt.
  • The word 'people' is a plural noun. So, it should be followed by a plural verb. (have)
  • Thus, 'have been warned' is the correct usage.
  • We need to use a verb warned because the doer of the verb warned is somebody else hence we need to use a past participle of the verb. As the warning has been given to the people by somebody else. Hence, the correct phrase is have been warned.
  • Therefore, option 4 is the correct answer.


Correct Sentence: People have been warned in advance about the coming economic crisis.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer. We needing to kept / a close eye on / the rising prices of fuel.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

We needing to kept / a close eye on / the rising prices of fuel.
questions.solution: The error lies in Part (1) of the sentence. 'Needing' is in continuous form. Any verb should be in Continuous form if there is a helping verb after the subject. We never use the third form of a verb after the infinitive 'to'. Correct sentence: We need to keep a close eye on the rising prices of fuel.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She has / not written / a single novel / by three years.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She has / not written / a single novel / by three years.
questions.solution: The error lies in 'By three years' part of the sentence. Instead of 'by' we will use 'for'. For is used in this case : For + period of time  -  for six years, for a week, for a month, for hours, for two hours.
